title: 1947年美国乡镇战地场景，复古胶片质感
prompt:
Create a 15-second ultra-photorealistic live-action war sequence set in the United States in 1947, designed to look like authentic historical footage captured on a 1940s film camera. The entire scene must feel grounded, documentary-like, raw, and physically realistic.
Environment: A rural American town in 1947 with wooden houses, old brick buildings, telephone poles, dirt roads, vintage American cars from the 1940s, wooden fences, farmland, and period-accurate street details. Overcast afternoon light, light fog, drifting smoke, dust in the air, damaged buildings, scattered debris, and a tense wartime atmosphere.
Characters: American soldiers wearing historically accurate late-1940s military uniforms, helmets, boots, and equipment. Civilians wear authentic 1940s American clothing. Natural faces, realistic skin texture, sweat, dirt, fatigue, and believable body movements.
0–3s — Establishing Shot:
Wide handheld shot of a quiet rural American street suddenly filled with smoke and confusion. Vintage 1940s vehicles are parked along the road while soldiers move quickly between wooden buildings. Civilians rush toward safer areas.
3–6s — Tension:
Camera moves through the street at shoulder height, following several soldiers as distant gunfire is heard. They immediately react and take cover behind a vintage vehicle and a brick wall. Their movements are cautious and realistic.
6–10s — Combat:
Fast handheld tracking shot as the soldiers move between cover while distant gunfire impacts the environment. Small pieces of wood, dust, and debris fall naturally from nearby impacts. Weapon recoil, movement, and body weight must be physically accurate. Keep the violence realistic and restrained.
10–13s — Human Moment:
Camera briefly focuses on a soldier helping an injured civilian move behind cover. Their breathing, facial expressions, body language, and movement should feel natural and unscripted.
13–15s — Final Shot:
Camera pulls back into a wide shot of the American town as smoke slowly moves through the street. Soldiers remain behind cover while vintage vehicles and damaged buildings fill the background. The scene ends with an authentic, tense 1940s documentary feeling.
Visual Style: Ultra-photorealistic live-action, authentic 1940s American environment, vintage 35mm film texture, subtle film grain, natural imperfections, realistic exposure, handheld documentary cinematography, muted historical color palette, realistic smoke and dust, natural shadows, accurate depth of field.
Physics: Strictly obey real-world gravity, momentum, inertia, friction, recoil, weight, collision physics, and human biomechanics. No exaggerated explosions, impossible movements, superhero behavior, or choreographed-looking combat.
Negative Prompt: modern buildings, modern cars, smartphones, modern clothing, modern weapons, futuristic technology, CGI appearance, video-game graphics, fantasy, superhero action, excessive explosions, excessive blood, gore, impossible physics, unrealistic recoil, slow-motion physics, distorted faces, extra limbs, floating objects, plastic skin, artificial-looking environments.
description: 把15秒切成带时间码的分镜（建立镜头、紧张、交火、人情瞬间、拉远），每段都写明机位运动。环境、人物、画面风格和物理规则各自成块，再配上较长的负面提示词，稳住1940年代35mm纪录片质感，动作也不会失真。
author: Ruzaina

title: 字母A到D依次变形为物体
prompt:
Create a 15-second animated educational video that teaches young children the letters A, B, C, and D.

The learning pattern for every letter must be:

LETTER → SOUND → OBJECT → PLAYFUL ACTION → OBJECT NAME

Target audience: children ages 3 to 6.

Visual style:
Use adorable rounded 3D characters, soft pastel colors, gentle facial expressions, and simple recognizable objects. Combine this with a premium minimalist technology aesthetic featuring clean white space, elegant composition, soft studio lighting, subtle reflections, smooth gradients, rounded geometry, crisp typography, and extremely polished transitions.

The animation should feel playful and child-friendly while remaining calm, uncluttered, and beautifully designed.

Use a clean off-white background with a different soft color glow behind each letter.

0:00–0:01 | Introduction
A small smiling star mascot bounces into the center of the screen.

Colorful letters briefly float around it.

Display the text:

“Let’s learn!”

The mascot taps the screen, creating a soft ripple that reveals the first letter.

0:01–0:04 | A is for Apple

Show a large uppercase “A” and smaller lowercase “a” beside it.
Use thick, rounded, highly readable typography.

The narrator says:

“A. A says ah. A is for Apple.”

The uppercase A gently inflates and transforms into a shiny red apple.

Its top point becomes the apple stem, and a small green leaf unfolds from the side.

The apple gains a cute smiling face and performs one soft bounce.

Display the word:

“APPLE”

Highlight the first letter A in red.

Add a soft pop and a tiny crunchy sound.

0:04–0:07 | B is for Ball

The apple rolls across the screen and leaves behind a curved red trail.

The trail loops twice and forms a large uppercase “B,” with a lowercase “b” appearing beside it.
The narrator says:

“B. B says buh. B is for Ball.”

The two rounded sections of the B expand and merge into a colorful striped ball.

The ball bounces twice with playful squash-and-stretch animation.

Display the word:

“BALL”

Highlight the first letter B in blue.

Synchronize each bounce with a soft musical note.

0:07–0:10 | C is for Cat

On its final bounce, the ball stretches into a curved shape and becomes a large uppercase “C.”

A lowercase “c” slides gently into place beside it.

The narrator says:
“C. C says kuh. C is for Cat.”

The C rotates and becomes the curled tail of a cute orange cat.

The rest of the cat forms from soft rounded shapes.

The cat stretches, blinks, and gives one gentle wave with its paw.

Display the word:

“CAT”

Highlight the first letter C in orange.

Add a quiet and friendly “meow.”

0:10–0:13 | D is for Duck

The cat’s tail uncurls and transforms into the curved side of a large uppercase “D.”

A lowercase “d” pops up beside it.

The narrator says:

“D. D says duh. D is for Duck.”
The straight line of the D becomes the duck’s neck.

The curved section becomes its round yellow body.

A small orange beak and two tiny wings pop into place.

The duck waddles forward, flaps its wings, and gives one cheerful quack.

Display the word:

“DUCK”

Highlight the first letter D in yellow.

Add tiny water ripples beneath its feet.

0:13–0:15 | Recap

The apple, ball, cat, and duck slide into four clean rounded tiles.

Place their letters above them:

“A  B  C  D”

The mascot returns and points to each object as they bounce once in sequence.

Narrator:
“A, B, C, D. Great job!”

Finish with the text:

“Great job!”

Use a small sparkle animation and a warm musical chime.

Animation requirements:

Keep each letter fully visible for a moment before it transforms.

Show uppercase and lowercase versions clearly.

Make every object instantly recognizable.

Use smooth shape morphing so children can visually understand how the letter becomes the object.

Maintain stable spelling, clean letterforms, accurate object shapes, and consistent character design.

Use gentle squash-and-stretch, soft motion blur, subtle shadows, polished lighting, and precisely synchronized sound effects.
Avoid fast camera movement, cluttered backgrounds, harsh colors, tiny text, warped letters, random symbols, duplicated objects, scary expressions, or overly complex transformations.

The final video should feel cute, educational, memorable, calming, and exceptionally polished.
description: 每个字母都遵循固定的五步模式（字母、发音、物体、动作、名称），并按三秒一段的时间码排布。字母与物体之间用连续形变衔接，提示词写明旁白台词、高亮颜色和音效，并用否定约束防止字母扭曲和背景杂乱。

title: 动漫双人被惊吓后害羞脸红
prompt:
2D anime | romantic comedy | cel-shaded, clean line art, dark blue night palette.
Multishot, 6 shots. Cuts only at the specified points.

CHARACTERS
HANA: wavy shoulder-length dark red hair, oversized gray cardigan with one button missing, a bandage on her index finger. 160 cm.
YUTO: neat black hair with a small bed-head tuft at the back, navy hoodie with a pilled sleeve, glasses pushed up on his forehead. 178 cm.

LOCATION
Dark living room at night. They share one sofa under a single fleece blanket. A TV off-frame in front of them is the only light source, flickering blue on their faces. A bowl of popcorn between them.

SUBTITLES
Spoken dialogue is in Japanese. English subtitles are burned into the image as on-screen text only — they are never spoken aloud. Style: white sans-serif, thin black outline, one single line, bottom center of frame, 8% from the bottom edge. Each subtitle appears with its line and disappears at the cut. Subtitle text is shown inside 【】 brackets below; the brackets themselves are not displayed.

Shot 1 (0–2.5s) — Medium front shot of both, FOV 47, static.
Hana sits upright, arms crossed, smug smile, chin raised. Yuto beside her grips a cushion with both hands, already tense.
Hana (spoken, Japanese): 「全然怖くないし。」
On-screen subtitle: 【I'm not scared at all.】
HARD CUT

Shot 2 (2.5–5s) — Close-up on Yuto, FOV 29, slow push-in ending on his eyes.
His pupils shrink to tiny dots, a vertical column of blue shade lines drops over his upper face, sweat drop on his temple. He swallows, the cushion squeezed flat. No subtitle in this shot.
HARD CUT

Shot 3 (5–8s) — Medium front shot, FOV 47, static.
A violent white flash from the TV and a loud sting. Both jump. Clear gag faces: mouths huge and wavy, eyes white, hair standing in spikes. The popcorn bowl flips and popcorn bursts upward like confetti. Two small white ghost-shaped souls slip out of their open mouths.
Hana and Yuto (spoken, Japanese): 「ぎゃああああっ！」
On-screen subtitle: 【AAAAAAH!】
HARD CUT

Shot 4 (8–10.5s) — Wide shot, FOV 63, static.
They are clutching each other tightly, trembling, their outlines drawn with shaky wobbling lines. Popcorn rains down on them. The souls drift back into their mouths. No subtitle in this shot.
HARD CUT

Shot 5 (10.5–13s) — Two-shot close-up, profile, FOV 29, static.
Silence. They slowly realize how close they are, faces a hand apart. Both blush deep red at the same time. A tiny comic sparkle pops between them. They let go and shuffle apart in short jerky movements. No subtitle in this shot.
HARD CUT

Shot 6 (13–15s) — Close-up on Hana, three-quarter front, FOV 29, static.
Normal detailed anime face: cheeks red, eyes sliding sideways, lips pouting. One popcorn kernel stuck in her hair.
Hana (spoken, Japanese): 「…今のはノーカン。」
On-screen subtitle: 【...That one doesn't count.】
She pulls the blanket up over her nose. End on her eyes peeking above the blanket.

LIGHTING
Only light source is the off-frame TV: flickering cool blue 8500K, with a single white flash in shot 3. Deep shadows in the room.

Sound: No score. Production audio only — faint TV dialogue murmur, a sharp horror sting, popcorn scattering, fabric rustle, double scream, then near silence and a soft blanket rustle. All voices in Japanese only.

Characters keep the same face, hair and wardrobe in every shot. Gag faces are clear, exaggerated super-deformed expressions, then return to the normal detailed anime face. Clean consistent line art, consistent lighting between shots. Subtitles stay in the same position, size and style in every shot, spelled exactly as written. The room contains only the sofa, the blanket and the popcorn bowl.
description: 提示词先写明镜头数、时间点和硬切，并规定字幕只作为画面文字出现、不被朗读。它把夸张的搞笑表情定义为短暂状态，之后回到正常的脸，同时在每个镜头里重复相同的发型、服装和电视光源，让角色在切换中保持一致。

title: 电梯里的动漫剑客与 CUT THE LINE 字样
prompt:
Create one complete 15-second, 16:9 high-energy anime music video with synchronized original music, vocals, combat sounds, visuals, and kinetic typography.

STYLE: pure 2D cel animation fused with tactile torn-paper collage. Use only ink black, warning red, and dirty paper white. Strong line art, flat shadows, halftone printing, photocopy grain, fibrous torn edges, dry ink, and brief print misregistration. Hard rhythmic cuts only—no fades or soft transitions.

CHARACTER: one consistent androgynous anime swordfighter with angular hair, narrow eyes, wrapped forearms, heavy boots, a long asymmetrical coat, and one chipped half-length broken sword. Keep the same face, body, costume, sword, and voice throughout. Enemies appear only as abstract ink-and-paper shadows.

MUSIC: original K-pop hip-hop × cyber-grunge micro-song, 128 BPM, minor key. Dry kick, metallic half-time snare, rapid controlled hi-hats, distorted metal pluck, photocopier percussion, descending 808, and sword impacts. Close neutral rap vocal expands into a melodic chant Hook. End with a sword ring, bass strike, short vocal tail, and clean stop.

LYRICS:

“Cracked steel, black seal, I carve through the night”

“Red tear, no fear, every scar turns bright”

“Hear the fault line sing”

“Break again — I rise”

“Last edge — still alive”

“Cut the line”

“Still standing”

TIMELINE:

Shot 1, 0.0–1.5s: Inside a freight elevator, the fighter walks from layered darkness, broken sword held low. A boot lands on a red paper seam as the camera pushes in. Readable paper-white text: “CUT THE LINE.” The sword tears through the letters and opens the next shot.

Shot 2, 1.5–3.2s: Low lateral tracking through concrete pillars. The fighter plants one foot, pivots from the shoulder, and sweeps the broken blade through an abstract red paper shadow. Readable black text across red posters: “NO CROWN.” The letters split with the sword arc.

Shot 3, 3.2–5.1s: The fighter runs diagonally, absorbs momentum against a wall with the forearm and shoulder, then rebounds in the opposite direction. Coat opens from the force. Text: “CUT THE LINE.” Wall contact tears the phrase; landing snaps it back together.

Shot 4, 5.1–6.7s: Extreme close-up and first still point. The fighter freezes; only pupils, breathing, and one coat edge move. The broken sword fills the foreground. On black, readable white text: “BREAK AGAIN.” A red duplicate shifts behind it during the rising Pre-hook, followed by a half-beat black frame.

Shot 5, 6.7–8.6s: Overhead view of an iron stair platform. The fighter drops from a safe low ledge, absorbs the landing through knees and hips, then rises into a diagonal guard. Red paper cracks radiate from the boot. “BREAK AGAIN” divides into three panels that fold back into one frame.

Shot 6, 8.6–10.7s: The fighter grips a railing, rotates ninety degrees, releases, and advances. The long coat sweeps across the foreground while the broken sword cuts a red paper silhouette. Readable wall text: “LAST EDGE.” The coat hides and then reveals the intact phrase.

Shot 7, 10.7–12.6s: Static rooftop shot and second still point. The fighter stands beneath a steel sign frame, blade angled down. Only breath, hair, coat hem, and wrist move. Large red text on black: “STILL STANDING.” Three torn panels briefly show the same eye, sword hand, and full silhouette without cloning the character.

Shot 8, 12.6–15.0s: The fighter surges forward and swings the broken blade upward. The sword splits the entire frame into two paper halves and cleaves a towering ink shadow, exposing dirty-white sky. The fighter completes a pivot and freezes facing camera. Huge readable text: “STILL STANDING.” Red and white print layers align on the final bass strike, then hard cut to black.

TYPOGRAPHY: ultra-bold condensed English capitals behaving like physical paper and wall print. Use only “CUT THE LINE,” “NO CROWN,” “BREAK AGAIN,” “LAST EDGE,” and “STILL STANDING.” Show each phrase clearly before tearing or shifting it. No subtitles, random letters, logos, brands, watermarks, or gibberish.

LOCKS: exactly one protagonist, one broken sword, one costume, and one voice. Preserve anatomy, hands, grip, mouth shapes, cloth physics, and spatial continuity. No repaired sword, extra people, extra weapons, glossy 3D, live action, pastel colors, excessive camera shake, or hand touching the lens. Finish decisively on the final beat and hard cut to black.
description: 将配色锁定为墨黑、警示红和纸白，并加入撕纸拼贴、网点与复印颗粒质感，形成印刷品般的画面。逐镜头时间线配合固定的文字、主角、武器和服装描述，并以硬切节奏保持人物与字幕前后一致。

prompt:
Experimental contemporary dance combined with TouchDesigner-style dynamic body tracking, generated as one complete uninterrupted continuous shot with no deliberate cuts.

A vast brutalist underground hall with a polished dark concrete floor, enormous vertical pillars, and one single rectangular ceiling light illuminating the center. The surrounding architecture gradually disappears into darkness. A male dancer with a shaved head, loose black trousers, and a fitted sleeveless top performs alone beneath the light. Preserve the brutalist geometry and the dancer as the sole performer.

The choreography combines slow controlled tension with sudden mechanical releases: sweeping circular arm movements, deep forward lunges, asymmetric shoulder rotations, sharp elbow extensions, backward arches, rapid half-turns, one-knee drops, and long diagonal reaches across the floor. His body repeatedly expands into wide sculptural poses and contracts tightly around the torso.

The camera constantly explores the performance geometry while remaining a single continuous move: extreme low angles close to the floor, overhead perspectives, slow circular tracking, profile close-ups, fast lateral travel, and sudden dolly pull-backs, all fluidly connected and precisely synchronized to the choreography. No shot cuts.

[Style — TouchDesigner-style real-time computer vision body-tracking visualization]

Apply sophisticated real-time body tracking densely and continuously throughout the entire clip. Glowing electric-blue and amber tracking nodes lock precisely onto the dancer's joints, hands, elbows, shoulders, knees, ankles, and torso, connected by thin geometric lines that dynamically stretch, collapse, and reorganize with every movement. Hands generate flowing vector trails. Rapid movements leave temporary wireframe echoes of previous body positions, creating layered geometric sculptures in space. During turns, circular tracking rings rotate around the torso; during floor movements, perspective grids expand outward across the concrete. As intensity rises, tracked coordinates, fragmented polygons, kinetic curves, and translucent skeletal structures accumulate around him, always responding precisely to his body. Keep the dancer visible and never obscure him with filled graphics.

Required CV overlay structure, visible continuously: 12-20 hollow axis-aligned rectangular tracking boxes at once, thin 1-2px electric-blue or amber strokes, absolutely no fill and no translucent color blocks. Maintain four clearly separated size tiers at every stable moment: 2-4 large local boxes, 3-5 medium local boxes, 3-5 small local boxes, and 4-6 visibly tiny micro boxes. Vary wide and tall rectangles. Every box tracks only a local body fragment or local motion region; never enclose the whole dancer, whole body, or whole head. The largest box covers no more than one quarter of the visible subject area. Micro-box area is at most 1/32 of the largest box. All box centers are visibly displaced; no concentric or near-concentric rectangle rings. On each audible downbeat or strong accent, replace, resize, jump, or relocate roughly 30-50% of the boxes to new local fragments while retaining the total count and all four size tiers.

Add thin straight topological connection lines linking displaced box corners and centers into a flexible star/network graph, alongside the joint-node skeleton. Add small clean monospace four-digit numeric IDs and [x, y] coordinate labels beside boxes; IDs and coordinates visibly randomize rapidly on every frame like a live CV debug console. Add optional sparse pixel samples and a subtle center crosshair only if they remain secondary.

Inside selected small and micro boxes only, show a true photographic negative of the exact underlying moving pixels, clipped precisely to each selected box's inner edge. Everything outside those selected small/micro rectangles, including large and medium box interiors, remains normal positive color. Rotate the negative windows across successive musical downbeats so different small/micro boxes take turns switching positive-to-negative and negative-to-positive. Never apply global negative, global monochrome, full-screen flashing, exposure pulsing, or strobing. Negative pixels must not bleed beyond the selected box interiors.

Audio is generated by the video model in sync with the visuals: instrumental experimental techno at 128 BPM, deep industrial kick, dry metallic percussion, pulsating distorted bass, and short bursts of synthetic noise. No vocals, no spoken voice, no lyrics. Every major beat drives the tracking-box changes, local negative-window switches, node pulses, trail persistence, and camera movement; the music and visual rhythm are tightly synchronized.

Final beat: the dancer suddenly stops in a wide asymmetric pose. All previous motion trails remain suspended around him for a brief moment, forming a large abstract three-dimensional wireframe sculpture of his movement history, then everything instantly disappears except the dancer under the ceiling light.

[Visual style — generated footage only]

Dark brutalist minimalism, high-contrast cinematic lighting, black and concrete-gray environment, electric-blue and amber tracking graphics, contemporary digital-art installation aesthetic. Apply a low-saturation desaturated underlying palette with natural teal/cyan cool shadows and warm highlights, strong 35mm film grain, high contrast with lifted blacks and preserved highlight detail, cinematic single-key or side/back lighting, shallow depth of field, subtle vignette, natural sharpness, and restrained highlight bloom. Keep film grain, grading, and optical artifacts confined to the generated footage; do not contaminate tracking lines, box outlines, nodes, IDs, or local negative masks.

HARD NEGATIVES: no solid-fill colored blocks, no filled overlays, no full-body or full-head bounding box, no silhouette-shaped or irregular boxes, no concentric rectangles, no same-size-only boxes, no fewer than 12 boxes, no missing micro boxes, no static IDs, no floating subtitles, no logo or watermark, no global black-and-white or desaturation, no global photographic negative, no full-screen black-white flash, no color strobe, no negative effect inside large or medium boxes, no negative bleed outside small/micro inner edges, no reference footage, no overlaid source footage, no extra performer, no deliberate shot cuts.

[Technical] 15 seconds, 16:9 horizontal, one continuous shot, 2K, cinematic motion, precise motion synchronization, generated instrumental audio.

Each letter fills with a different beautiful pattern, such as gradients, dots, stripes, floral shapes, and soft wing-like textures. Keep the word fully readable and centered. Let the audience admire the full word before the transformation begins.  0:04–0:09 This is the main highlight. The word “BUTTERFLY” transforms slowly and satisfyingly into the butterfly.  The transformation must be gradual, staged, and visually delicious to watch: The “B” gently opens outward and unfolds into the top wings. The “U” stretches and curves into one lower wing. The first “T” and second “T” slim down and merge into the butterfly’s long body. The “E” softens and reshapes into decorative wing markings. The “R” curls upward into one antenna. The “F” reshapes into the second antenna with a playful wobble. The “L” and “Y” arc outward and become the final wing edges and tail details.  Important: Do not transform everything at once. Let each part morph one after another in a smooth chain reaction. The letters should bend, curl, unfurl, rotate, stretch, and softly glide into their new forms. The child should still sense the original word during the transformation. Use sparkling trails, flowing color transfer, and soft elastic motion to make it deeply satisfying. The morph should feel magical, clear, and creatively intelligent.  0:09–0:11 The butterfly is now a fully formed cute stylized cartoon butterfly. It has lovely colorful wings, a tiny smiling face, big friendly eyes, and soft funny charm. It flutters gently in a playful little loop, hovers above a flower, almost sneezes from pollen in a cute funny moment, then recovers and smiles. Show the word “Butterfly” below it briefly for reinforcement. The narrator repeats: “Butterfly.”  0:11–0:14 This is the second major highlight. The entire animated scene slowly transforms into a realistic world.  The butterfly flaps its wings in slow motion. With each flap, realism increases gradually: its wing textures become more detailed the colors gain natural variation the body becomes more lifelike the flowers gain realistic petals and depth the background softens into a real sunlit garden the lighting becomes natural and golden the air gains subtle movement and realistic depth of field  This transformation should feel breathtaking, seamless, and immersive. Do not cut abruptly from cartoon to realistic. Instead, let the animated world gently bloom into reality in layers. The viewer should feel they are witnessing imagination turn into nature.  0:14–0:15 End on a beautiful realistic butterfly resting on a real flower in warm sunlight. Display the text: “B is for Butterfly” The narrator says warmly: “B is for Butterfly.” The butterfly gently flutters once, then lifts off lightly.  Style and quality requirements: Keep the letter B and the word “BUTTERFLY” clearly readable before and during transformation. Make the word-to-animal morph slow, rich, and visually rewarding. Make the stylized-to-realistic transformation equally slow, smooth, and magical. Use polished motion design, soft easing, beautiful color transitions, gentle humor, and strong visual clarity. Maintain a child-friendly tone throughout. Use clean typography, stable spelling, and seamless morphing.  Audio direction: Use cheerful, soft, magical music. Add delicate sparkles, soft pops, flutter sounds, a tiny comedic sniffle or sneeze, and a gentle emotional swell during the realism transition. Voiceover should be warm, clear, slow, and easy for children to follow.  Avoid: rushed transformations, unreadable letters, clutter, hard cuts, scary expressions, excessive camera motion, chaotic effects, or anything visually confusing for children.
description: 变形按部位逐个进行，每个字母依次重塑，原单词在过程中始终可辨认。第二段放慢蝴蝶的每次振翅，每一下都增加一层真实感，让卡通世界过渡为真实花园，中间没有硬切。
author: Umesh

title: 年轻女子在咖啡馆发现初雪
prompt: Create a dreamy 15-second Korean winter vlog. A young woman sits inside a minimalist café holding a hot drink when she notices the first snow beginning outside. She excitedly grabs her phone, walks outside, catches a snowflake on her sleeve, and looks up smiling. Soft Korean winter atmosphere, warm café interior contrasting with cold blue outdoors, realistic snow physics, handheld vlog footage, cinematic and natural, no text.
description: 按时间顺序写出一连串动作：在咖啡馆喝饮品、拿出手机、走到户外、雪花落在袖子上、抬头微笑，15秒内节奏清楚。明确写出手持 vlog 拍摄风格，并对比温暖室内与冷蓝户外的色调，让运镜和调色有明确方向；结尾加上不要字幕，避免画面出现文字。
author: Snow

title: 车后座浣熊与猴子的薯片爆开
prompt: A cinematic video inside the back seat of a moving car with beige leather interior On the right a young woman with medium-length brown hair, wearing a yellow knitted sweater and blue jeans is holding a blue bag of potato chips Sitting on the left is a fluffy raccoon and a small capuchin monkey is resting close to the raccoon The woman offers a chip to the animals but as the raccoon reaches into the bag chips accidentally burst into the air and scatter all over the backseat including one landing on the raccoon's head The woman reacts with surprise and then bursts into laughter while the monkey looks around curious and playful Photorealistic soft natural lighting, vibrant colors.
description: 提示词先固定场景、人物位置和服装，再按开头、中段、结尾三个节拍推进，让薯片炸开成为清晰的笑点。柔和自然光和写实描述让动物显得可信。
author: Lavinia

title: 雨夜纸箱里猫咪守护被遗弃的小狗
prompt:
Popo, a cat, finds a puppy abandoned in a cardboard box under the eaves. At first, Popo acts cold and indifferent, but when heavy rain begins, the cat bravely shields the puppy from the storm and spends the night keeping it warm beneath its belly.

By the next morning, a bond has formed between them. They begin facing the harsh life of stray animals together—Popo suppressing its own hunger to give the puppy its prey, even sneaking into a supermarket in search of food. Eventually, with the kindness and help of people around them, the two manage to get something to eat. As they cuddle together beneath the setting sun, they develop a deep and genuine bond that transcends species.
description: 提示词按时间顺序写成一个短故事：相遇、暴雨、清晨、觅食、日落。给动物主角起名让主体保持一致，每个段落都写明情绪变化，所以 15 秒的片段能装下完整叙事。
author: Zarnish

title: 厨师在面粉中用刀压饺子面团
prompt:
The chef prepares a supple dumpling dough, rolls it into a very large thin circular wrapper on a lightly floured wooden board, then mixes seasoned pork filling with cubes of chilled gelatinized stock, showing convincing close-ups of the ingredients, hands, textures, flour, moisture, and utensils.
A generous mound of filling is placed in the center, then the chef slowly lifts and pleats the enormous wrapper around it, creating dozens of small folds while rotating the dumpling by hand until the top closes into a neat twisted knot and the whole dumpling visibly sags with realistic weight.
The giant dumpling is transferred carefully into a wide bamboo steamer lined with cabbage leaves, the lid closes, steam escapes naturally around the rim, then after cooking the lid is lifted and dense steam reveals the now-translucent, glossy dumpling sitting intact inside.
The chef slides it into a shallow serving bowl, places ginger and black vinegar beside it, then punctures the top gently with chopsticks so a large amount of hot golden broth visibly pours from inside the dumpling into the bowl while the delicate skin remains mostly intact.
Finish with a close-up of the chef opening the dumpling further and spooning up the broth, pork filling, and thin wrapper together, emphasizing realistic steam, liquid movement, chopstick sounds, bamboo creaks, ceramic clinks, and kitchen ambience, with absolutely no spoken language or music.
description: 提示词采用编号分段的分镜写法，每段只写一个动作并给出明确结尾，使多段连续生成保持连贯。明确列出声音细节并禁止人声和音乐，让音轨只保留厨房环境声。
author: cocktail peanut

title: 克利奥帕特拉在王座上迎接披萨外卖员
prompt:
0:00–0:04 — Medium shot inside a golden pyramid chamber. CLEOPATRA sits on her throne looking majestic. A modern pizza delivery guy in helmet and red jacket suddenly walks in holding a large pizza box.
0:04–0:07 — Cleopatra stands up, points at the box and starts singing in a dramatic royal voice: “Pizza man, pizza man… bring the cheese across the sand!” while doing slow Egyptian hand waves.
0:07–0:10 — The delivery guy tries hard to stay professional and say “That’ll be 12 dollars,” but his lips start trembling.
0:10–0:13 — He can’t hold it and bursts out laughing, almost dropping the pizza.
0:13–0:15 — Cleopatra freezes mid-hand-wave, looks at him, and completely cracks up too. Both are laughing while the pizza box tilts dangerously.
description: 按时间戳分段规定每个反应的时机，台词用引号单独标出，让口型同步有明确的对白可依。把皇家殿堂与现代外卖员放在一起，在台词出现前就建立了笑点。
author: 𝐌
